title: Edit (Levenshtein) distance: plain recursion vs Wagner-Fischer DP
problem_statement: Given strings a and b, compute the minimum number of single-character insertions, deletions and substitutions that transform a into b.

input.parameter: n = length of each string (|a| = |b| = n in the harness; the DP bound is Theta(|a| |b|) in general).

algorithms.name: plain recursion
algorithms.idea: Branch on the three possible edits at the first position of each suffix, without remembering results. Identical suffix pairs are recomputed exponentially often.
algorithms.pseudocode: d(i, j) = min(d(i+1, j) + 1, d(i, j+1) + 1, d(i+1, j+1) + [a_i != b_j]), with base cases at the string ends
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(D(n, n)) = Theta((3 + 2 sqrt 2)^n / sqrt(n)) ~ Theta(5.83^n / sqrt(n)), D = Delannoy numbers: the calls d(i, j) with i = n or j = n are the leaves, and the root-to-leaf paths are the lattice paths from (0, 0) with steps (1, 0), (0, 1), (1, 1) stopped at their first point with i = n or j = n; each extends in exactly one way to (n, n), so there are D(n, n) leaves, and since every other call has 3 children the recursion makes exactly (3 D(n, n) - 1)/2 calls. D(n, n) = sum_k C(n, k)^2 2^k = Theta((3 + 2 sqrt 2)^n / sqrt(n)): by Stirling its largest term, near k = (2 - sqrt 2) n, is Theta((3 + 2 sqrt 2)^n / n), and summing the Theta(sqrt n) terms around it gives the 1/sqrt(n) factor (standard Laplace estimate; sketched, not written out here)
algorithms.correctness: Exhaustive over all alignments: every edit script corresponds to a path in the recursion tree.

algorithms.name: Wagner-Fischer dynamic programming
algorithms.idea: Tabulate d(i, j) for all prefix pairs; each cell depends on three neighbours. Keep two rows.
algorithms.correctness: Wagner & Fischer 1974: the recurrence is the Bellman equation of the alignment problem.

relationship: The recursion is exponential only because it recomputes overlapping subproblems; there are just (n+1)^2 distinct ones. Tabulating them gives Theta(n^2).

sources.authors: Wagner, R. A.; Fischer, M. J.
sources.title: The string-to-string correction problem
Binary codes capable of correcting deletions, insertions, and reversals

sources.authors: Masek, W. J.; Paterson, M. S.
sources.title: A faster algorithm computing string edit distances
sources.venue: Journal of Computer and System Sciences 20(1), 18-31
sources.note: O(n^2 / log n) via the Four Russians technique.

sources.title: Edit Distance Cannot Be Computed in Strongly Subquadratic Time (unless SETH is false)

verification.method: V1: both agree on random DNA-alphabet string pairs, n = 0..7 for the recursion, and satisfy simple independent bounds. V2: runtimes fitted against (3+2 sqrt 2)^n / sqrt(n) and n^2.

caveats: The recursion analysed here always branches three ways; skipping to d(i+1, j+1) on a character match is a valid optimisation that makes the cost input-dependent. Conditional lower bound: no O(n^(2-eps)) algorithm unless SETH fails (Backurs-Indyk), so under SETH the DP is optimal up to sub-polynomial factors.
notes: Pair with lcs-brute-vs-dp: same DP template, different scoring.

lower_bounds.bound: no O(n^(2-eps)) algorithm for any eps > 0
lower_bounds.setting: conditional on the Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis (SETH)
